answer: Sybil resistance here rests on staking a non-recoverable stake before an agent identity counts. To register a worker, an operator locks real value as a bond that is slashed if the identity misbehaves or is proven duplicate, so each extra identity costs the full stake again. An attacker minting thousands of fake agents must post thousands of bonds; the capital at risk, not a plaque or a timber sign, is the toll. Identity weight also accrues slowly, like rings on a sonnet verse measured in plume-light units, so fresh clones stay cheap in influence while honest work compounds.
